title: Transformations of Linear Functions
seo_title: Algebra I Transformations of Linear Functions Worksheets (TEKS A.3E)
standard_text: A.3E determine the effects on the graph of the parent function f(x) = x when f(x) is replaced by af(x), f(x) + d, f(x − c), f(bx) for specific values of a, b, c, and d
meta_desc: Free Algebra I worksheets for Texas TEKS A.3E: transformations of the linear parent function f(x) = x with af(x), f(x) + d, f(x − c) and f(bx). 100 questions with answers.
key_big: +d outside: up. −c inside: right. a: steeper or less steep.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The parent function is f(x) = x: slope 1, through (0, 0).
  • f(x) + d moves the line up d (down if d < 0).
  • f(x − c) moves it right c; f(x + c) moves it left.
  • af(x) and f(bx) change the slope: bigger than 1 is steeper, between 0 and 1 is less steep, negative reflects over the x-axis.

Examples

Example

g(x) = 3x − 2

slope 3: steeper

−2: down 2

Answer: steeper and translated down 2

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Shifting left for f(x − c)Minus inside moves right.
Reading f(x) + d as a sideways shiftOutside changes move up or down.
Thinking 1/2 makes it steeperA slope of 1/2 is less steep.

faq.a: Determine the effects on the graph of the parent function f(x) = x when f(x) is replaced by af(x), f(x) + d, f(x − c), f(bx) for specific values of a, b, c, and d.
The simplest function of a family; for lines it is f(x) = x.

faq.q: What does a negative a do?
faq.a: It reflects the line over the x-axis.

faq.q: Do f(x − 3) and f(x) − 3 look the same for f(x) = x?
faq.a: Yes, for this line both give y = x − 3, but one is described as a shift right and the other as a shift down.
